name: Stein Erik Hagen
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Stein Erik Hagen founded the discount supermarket Rimi with his father in the 1970s.
In 2014 Hagen appointed his daughter, billionaire Caroline Marie Hagen Kjos, to take over the reins of his family's investment company Canica AS.
Caroline, now chairman, owns a majority of the holdings, though Stein Erik maintains a seat on the board.
He created Canica upon selling his stake in Rimi in 1998, after the chain had merged with Sweden's ICA; it later merged with Dutch retailer Ahold.
Canica has investments across Scandinavia, including consumer goods manufacturer Orkla, which Hagen chairs, and hardware store chain Jernia.

name: Louis Le Duff
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2014-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026)
forbes_bio: Louis Le Duff got his start when he opened a combined restaurant-bakery in a Quebec ski resort while studying abroad for his MBA.
In 1976, he took the concept back to France and opened the first Brioche Dorée bakery in Brittany with just $2,000.
Groupe Le Duff now operates more than 1,000 bakery and restaurant locations, including La Madeleine French eateries chain in the U.S. and Del Arte in France.
The company's biggest business is Bridor, which produces high-quality breads and pastries for hotels, restaurants and catering services in more than 100 countries.
Le Duff also owns frozen food maker Gourming, and he owned the Bruegger's Bagels chain from 2011 until 2017, when he sold it to Caribou Coffee Company.
forbes_facts: In the summer of 1970, when Le Duff studied at Columbia University in the City of New York, he worked night shifts at a French creperie on 3rd Street.

name: Joao Roberto Marinho
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2013-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Joao Roberto Marinho and his two billionaire brothers, Jose Roberto and Roberto Irineu, inherited control of Globo, Brazil's largest media group.
Their grandfather Irineu Marinho launched O Globo newspaper in 1925; he died 25 days after the first issue was published and his oldest son took over.
Globo Group includes Brazil's largest broadcaster, Rede Globo; Brazil's largest newspaper company and Globosat, Brazil's largest pay TV provider.
Joao Roberto worked at O Globo, one of Brazil's most influential newspapers. He held a number of positions before becoming vice president in 1982.
Joao Roberto is now the executive president of Grupo Globo and the chairman of the board of directors.
forbes_facts: The Marinho family contributed to the establishment of museums in Brazil such as Museum of Tomorrow, The Football Museum, and Museum of the Portuguese Language.

name: Ramesh Juneja
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Forbes annual (2018-2025); Hurun Global (2016-2026); Hurun India (2015-2019)
forbes_bio: Ramesh Juneja is chairman and director of Mankind Pharma, which he cofounded alongside his younger brother Rajeev Juneja in 1995.
The company sells generic drugs including antibiotics and treatments for cardiovascular diseases in over two dozen markets worldwide.
The moguls took the company public in India in May 2023, raising 43.3 billion rupees ($529 million).
His U.K.-educated son Arjun is the company's chief operating officer. He led Mankind's entry into international markets, including the U.S.
The company also makes popular brands of condoms and pregnancy test kits.
forbes_facts: Bollywood veteran Amitabh Bachchan is Mankind's brand ambassador.
Juneja and his younger brother were born on the same date, ten years apart.

name: Denis O'Brien
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2008-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Wikidata (2020)
forbes_bio: Denis O'Brien founded Digicel, a mobile phone network provider that operates in the Caribbean, Asia Pacific and Central America.
O'Brien made a fortune selling his Irish mobile outfit, Esat Telecom Group, to British Telecom Group in 2000 for $2.8 billion.
He has investments in energy companies and resorts on the Iberian Peninsula.
In 2019, O'Brien sold his stake in Independent News and Media to Mediahuis, losing hundreds of millions of Euros on his investment.
O'Brien made another media industry exit in 2021 by selling Communicorps, a radio company, to Bauer Media
forbes_facts: O'Brien, whose mother was a political activist, cofounded the Front Line Defenders to protect and provide emergency support for human rights activists in danger.

appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2023); Forbes annual (2022)
forbes_bio: Zhang Lei is the founder and CEO of Hillhouse Capital Management.
Zhang holds and MBA and M.A. in international relations from Yale University.
Zhang holds a B.A. from Renmin University in Beijing, where he is vice chairman of the board of trustees.

name: Sanjeev Bikhchandani
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2019-2025); Hurun Global (2018-2026); Hurun India (2015-2022)
forbes_bio: Indian internet pioneer, Sanjeev Bikhchandani, draws his wealth from listed Info Edge (India).
Info Edge owns portals for job search (naukri.com), matrimony (jeevansathi.com); real estate (99acres.com) and education (shiksha.com).
It also owns stakes in online food delivery outfit Zomato and insurance marketplace, policybazaar.com. Both companies went public in 2021.
Bikhchandani, who studied at the premier Indian Institute of Management, Ahmedabad, is founder and executive vice-chairman of Info Edge.
forbes_facts: He cofounded and funded Ashoka University, a liberal arts institution, which is located in the north Indian state of Haryana.

name: Stephan Crétier
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026)
forbes_bio: Stephan Crétier is the founder and CEO of GardaWorld, a Montreal-based private security and cash services firm.
He founded the business in 1995 with $25,000, which he raised by putting a second mortgage on his house.
He took the firm public on the Toronto Stock Exchange in 2003 and then took it private alongside private equity firm Apax Partners in 2012 at a $1.1 billion valuation.
In 2019, he recapitalized the firm with private equity firm BC Partners at a $3.9 billion valuation. Six years later, he took back a majority stake in a deal that valued the firm at $9.8 billion.
Besides its core security and cash services businesses, GardaWorld also owns intelligence platform Crisis24, cash management firm Sesami, and remote surveillance outfit ECAM.
forbes_facts: Crétier's first job was selling firecrackers at school at age 13.
Crétier trained as a baseball umpire as a teenager, going on to umpire international tournaments and get scouted by Major League Baseball before stepping away at 25.

name: Zhang Li
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun China (2003-2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2026)
forbes_bio: Zhang Li is a co-founder of real estate developer Guangzhou R&F with Hong Kong billionaire Li Sze Lim; the duo set up the company in 1994.
He resigned as CEO at the end of 2023 months after reportedly admitting to paying bribes in San Francisco to obtain a building permit.
Zhang once worked in Guangzhou as the Secretary of Youth League Committee of Guangzhou 2nd Light Industry Bureau, as well as a hotel manager.
Zhang also owns a stake in Hong Kong-listed Kinetic Mines and Energy, a company he founded with son Johnson in 2006.

name: Wei Yin-Heng
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2010-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026); Hurun China (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Wei Yin-Heng and his three brothers, Ing-Chou, Yin-Chun and Ying-Chiao, started Tingyi in 1991.
Tingyi is now one of the largest producers of ready-to-drink tea and bottled water in China. It is also a major supplier to the country's instant-noodle market.
The family also controls the Dicos fried-chicken chain.
The family's private company, Ting Hsin, sold its 37.17% stake in Taipei 101, Taiwan's tallest building, to Itochu for $665 million in July 2018.
forbes_facts: Wei graduated from a local high school in Changhua County, central Taiwan, and never went to  college.

name: Tim Draper
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: A scion of a Silicon Valley investing dynasty, Tim Draper is a founding partner of venture capital firm Draper Fisher Jurvetson.
Draper has made hundreds of VC investments in companies including Tesla and Theranos, and has made a fortune investing in cryptocurrencies.
In 2014, he bought 29,656 bitcoins confiscated by U.S. Marshals from the shuttered Silk Road black market for $18.7 million, or just $632 per coin.

name: Yuri Gushchin
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2020); Forbes annual (2013-2018); Hurun Global (2020-2023)
forbes_bio: Yuri Gushchin gets the bulk of his fortune from United Confectioners, the biggest candy company in Russia.
During the Soviet era, Gushchin was an underground producer of consumer goods, particularly candy.
During Perestroika he became one of the first businessmen to legalize those operations.
After the 1998 Russian financial crisis, he bought a controlling stake in Moscow's biggest confectionary factories and created United Confectioners.
Gushchin leases out buildings near the Kremlin including Red October that used to belong to the candy company.
forbes_facts: He lives in Seychelles where he owns a luxury hotel called Savoy Resort and Spa. He also owns the Savoy Hotel in Moscow.

name: Laurie Tisch
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2018-2025); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Laurie Tisch's late father Bob (d. 2005) started Loews Corporation with his brother Laurence (d. 2003) as a New Jersey hotel venture in 1946.
Today, Loews is active in insurance, drilling rigs, natural gas pipelines, and hotels.
Laurie's mother Joan Tisch (d. 2017) was the largest individual Loews shareholder with a 6% stake. Laurie and her two siblings inherited her mother's stake.
In 1991, her father Bob bought a 50% stake in the New York Giants for $75 million.
Laurie's brother Steve Tisch is chairman and executive vice president of the NFL team, which FORBES values at $6.3 billion (net of debt).
forbes_facts: An avid art collector, Laurie Tisch is a trustee at the Whitney Museum of American Art in New York City.
In 2008, Tisch worked with then-New York Mayor Michael Bloomberg to launch NYC Green Carts, which provides fresh produce to "food deserts" throughout the city.

name: Vasily Shikin
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026); Hurun Global U40 (2026); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Vasily Shikin is chief technology officer of AI-powered advertising technology company AppLovin, which went public on the Nasdaq in 2021.
He served as AppLovin's vice president of engineering for eight years before being tapped as CTO in 2020.
Shikin is one of eight billionaires from AppLovin, including the company's cofounder and CEO Adam Foroughi.
Prior to joining AppLovin in 2012, Shikin worked for four years as a software engineer at Device Anywhere, a cloud-based platform for testing and monitoring mobile websites and apps.
Born in Russia, Shikin has a master's in mathematics from Saint-Petersburg State University.

name: Raghuvinder Kataria
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2020); Forbes annual (2015-2019); Hurun Global (2017-2026)
forbes_bio: Indian-born British citizen, Raghuvinder Kataria, chairs his Dubai investment firm Kataria Holdings.
An early telecom investor, he sold a minority stake in Sunil Mittal's Bharti Airtel at the stock's peak, cashing in an estimated $500 million.
During the 2009 Dubai downturn, he bought 2 buildings in Emaar Square in the central business district for $205 million.
forbes_facts: He also has stakes in Danish technology firm Vopium, a Skype rival and India's Dhanlaxmi Bank.
Kataria is a regular donor to the Al Jalila Foundation, a non-profit founded by Dubai ruler Sheikh Mohammed Bin Rashid Al Maktoum.
